title: Printer jam
text: The printer is eating Priya's final pitch deck, page by page, with audible joy. She looks about to commit a crime.

choices.result: You emerge with toner on your face and her deck intact. 'Don't make it weird,' she says. It's the nicest thing she's said all week.

choices.text: Email her the digital copy you kept
choices.result: 'You kept a backup of MY deck?' She looks suspicious, then grateful, then suspicious again.
You escape. Behind you, the printer sounds like it's winning.

title: Birthday cake
text: It's someone in Finance's birthday. There's a cake in the kitchen the size of a car tyre.

choices.text: Join in, sing badly, eat cake
choices.result: You sing the worst harmony the ninth floor has ever heard. People love it.

choices.text: Grab a slice for Noah in the corner
choices.result: Noah stares at the cake like nobody has ever brought him cake before. Possibly nobody has.
You hear the cheering from your desk. The spreadsheet does not cheer.

title: Surprise visit
text: Vaughn strolls the floor unannounced, asking random people 'what they're adding to Lighthouse.' He's heading your way.

choices.result: He nods, mildly impressed. 'Concise. I like concise.' You feel slightly dirty for enjoying that.
'Team player,' he says, like it's a diagnosis. Marcus, across the room, gives you a tiny nod.

choices.text: Pretend to be on a call
choices.result: You talk earnestly to nobody about 'synergies' until he leaves. Zara saw everything.

title: Wi-Fi outage
text: The office Wi-Fi dies. Forty people look up from their screens and remember the others exist.

choices.result: Without screens, ideas fly. Marcus says 'that's solid' twice in an hour, a new record.
Kai is delighted. 'Analogue hour! Pencils for everyone!'
The café is empty and the soup is excellent.

title: Sudden downpour
text: A storm hits right as people are heading out. Zara is standing at the door without an umbrella, staring at the sky like it owes her money.

choices.result: It's a small umbrella. You both get half-soaked and laugh the whole way to the station.

choices.text: Lend it to her and run for it
choices.result: You arrive home drenched. She texts a photo of your umbrella with a heart emoji.

title: Spotted a mistake
text: You notice a wrong number in the forecast that went out to the whole floor this morning. Noah built that model.

choices.result: He fixes it in four minutes and sends a quiet correction. 'Thank you for not doing that in public,' he whispers.
You're right, and everyone knows you're right. Nobody thanks you for it.
Someone else spots it on Thursday. It causes a small, avoidable panic.

title: Lunch crowd
text: A group from Marketing invites you to their legendary Thursday lunch.

choices.result: Three hours of gossip compressed into one. You learn who actually runs this building (it's the receptionist).
They say 'next time' in a way that might mean it.

title: Fire drill
text: The alarm goes off. Fire drill. Everyone files out to the car park. Priya is standing alone, still holding her laptop.

choices.text: Stand with Priya and talk shop
choices.result: You argue about the Lighthouse rollout for twenty minutes. It's the most fun either of you has had all week.
Zara has a running commentary on everyone's fire-drill outfits. It's devastating.
Ten quiet minutes in the sun. You hadn't realised how much you needed that.

title: 5pm request
text: At 4:58pm an urgent request lands from Vaughn's office: 'Need this tonight.'

choices.result: Done by 10pm. Vaughn replies 'k.' One letter. For four hours.

choices.text: Reply with a realistic deadline: tomorrow noon
choices.result: Silence, then 'fine.' Kai overhears and silently applauds.
Marcus handles it. 'Next time, push back yourself,' he says, not unkindly.

title: The office plant
text: The big fern by the lift is dying. Nobody owns it. Everybody has opinions.

choices.result: Within two weeks it's thriving. People start calling it 'your fern.' Kai draws it a tiny crown.
Fate, it turns out, does not water plants.

title: Coffee run
text: You're heading out for coffee. Someone shouts, 'Get one for me!' Then everyone does.

choices.result: Eleven coffees, two trips, one burned hand. You're a legend by lunchtime.
Your coffee is perfect. The looks you get on the way back are less so.

title: Shout-out
text: Marcus mentions your work in the weekly update. Publicly. With your name in bold.

choices.text: Thank him and share the credit with Zara
choices.result: Zara grins. 'Sharing credit? Who raised you? Lovely.'
You read it three times. Then a fourth, just to be sure.

title: Empty seat
text: Noah is eating alone at the far end of the café again, reading a statistics paper for fun.

choices.result: He explains Bayesian priors using a sandwich. You understand maybe half. He glows the whole time.
He waves back, startled and pleased.

title: Office gossip
text: Someone in the kitchen asks you what you really think of Priya. Several ears lean in.

choices.text: 'She's the sharpest person on this floor.'
choices.result: It gets back to Priya within the hour. She says nothing. She brings you a coffee the next day.
It gets back to Priya within the hour too. She says nothing. That is much worse.
You start talking about the weather with the intensity of a meteorologist. It works.

title: Feeling rough
text: You wake up with a scratchy throat and the energy of a damp towel.

choices.result: Tea, blankets, half-speed emails. You're better by evening.
You make it through. Barely. Zara puts a lozenge on your keyboard without comment.

title: Ask a question
text: In the all-team meeting, nobody asks a question. The silence stretches. You have one.

choices.result: It's a good question. Marcus takes notes. Two people message you afterwards: 'I was wondering that too.'
Someone else asks it a week later and gets the credit.
